title: Going Deeper Into What's Happening Here
content_md: It's time to spill it, lay bare all the details of what's going on here so folks can judge and (HA!) not complain because there's no comment form As if anyone actually reads this site, something I severely doubt.. I could put a comment form in and not have it do anything, kind of like the vent in my office ceiling that isn't actually connected to the furnace so I freeze every winter. I'll leave that feature for last. ## In a nutshell, this is the setup: - Current iteration of this site runs plain ol' HTML/CSS/JavaScript in Github Pages with one of my most coveted domains (say it with me, and clap with each word for emphasis: NOT. FOR. SALE.). When I saw humm.us was available as a domain, I think I dented my laptop by violently hitting the BUY button. Since registering the domain, I've been hit on by 5 companies that tried to get it from me. Not happening. - Data storage is in a MariaDB database running on a Raspberry Pi inside my house. - A bash script builds a JSON file from published posts in the database, which is copied to the site source tree before deployment. - An admin page in a separate (React) site that runs on my laptop manages "draft" and published post content. - A small Node.js API provides the CRUD action between the admin page and the database. - Claude helped me a bit with some of the coding. I had to correct a lot of it, but I have to say it did speed things along. - Page content is all written and stored as Markdown. It's all translated to HTML on the fly when it's rendered. This is part of an ongoing experiment to see if a site can be fully managed locally and then easily deployed as a static website with no database backing it up, no admin control outside of my own laptop, no forms (I mentioned no comments already...want to say something, odds are good my email address is available on this site). And, considering it's being served at the moment as a Github Page, I can add *no monthly cost* to that list of "no"s. My data, I'm in control, 100% my code, no third party downloads (HTML5 APIs, baby! It's just me, an editor, and a web browser), and my design (watch me throw it out a week from now and do something else). ## AI...what? Yes, Claude did some coding here. Don't say "vibe coded". I actually know how to write HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Node.js APIs, etc. It's probably more accurate to say Claude *typed* some code. ## No React? Again, *what*? No React. Site's too small, I don't need the third party headaches, and besides, I can implement my own reactivity using JavaScript Proxy objects (I may post on that at some point, if for no other reason than I want to remember it). It's new/old school all the way, which is my favorite way to roll. I use React at work. For now, that's enough React. The admin site that I use locally to maintain posts is a small React site, but I plan to swap out React for something else, like perhaps something more vanilla. React's fine, but it's a lot of lifting for a tiny site. ## Shut up. You talk too much. I know.

title: Posts without a database
summary: How to have a website with posts but not have to connect it to a database
content_md:
I'm trying to add a page to my Github Pages site that shows "posts". I have some pretty strange criteria:  
  
- no database on the web ($$, configuation, etc...forget it)  
- post content must support markdown (no HTML in database tables)   
  
There seems to be one general way to handle this: local database, all posts in the database are pre-fetched and added to the React site somehow so they can be used to generate the "posts" page.  
  
### Pre-fetching?  
  
Pre-fetching is key here. That's where the database is queried up front to collect data, and then the data is stored in the site code where JavaScript can see it and process it when the site renders.  
  
If the posts are in a file in /public, they should be seen by the React code. I can then grab the file, read its contents, and loop through the items to build all of the posts. The react-markdown component appears to handle rendering just fine, so that leaves the actual pre-fetching.  
  
MariaDB supports rendering results as JSON. The mysql command line utility can connect to a remote database (it's inside my house, but not on the machine that's building/deploying the React site). Put the two together and you can query and render to JSON all on one command line.   
  
### What about security?  
  
What about it? I'm not sure security is much of an issue if there is no database being contacted, no comment forms to enter data, no DOS attack vectors that will drive up cloud database costs, etc. It's a static site with static data. I'm going to look into it, but I doubt I'll find anything that absolutely requires hand wringing.  
  
### SHIP IT  
  
Working on it.
